history.heading: Arabia Felix
paragraphs: Yemen, in the southwest of the Arabian Peninsula, was known to the Romans as Arabia Felix ("Fortunate Arabia") for its fertility and wealth from the incense trade. Ancient kingdoms such as Saba (Sheba), Qataban and Himyar flourished; the Marib Dam was an engineering marvel. Yemen adopted Islam in the 7th century.

The Zaydi imams, a branch of Shia Islam, ruled the northern highlands for about a thousand years. The Ottomans controlled parts of Yemen at times, and the port of Mocha gave its name to coffee, which was first widely traded from Yemen. Britain took Aden in 1839.

history.heading: Two Yemens and unification
paragraphs: North Yemen became independent from the Ottomans in 1918 under the imams; a 1962 revolution created a republic after a civil war in which Egypt and Saudi Arabia intervened. South Yemen won independence from Britain in 1967 and became the Arab world's only Marxist state. The two united in 1990 under Ali Abdullah Saleh. A civil war in 1994 ended with the north's victory.

history.heading: Civil war
paragraphs: Arab Spring protests forced Saleh to step down in 2012. In 2014 the Houthis, a Zaydi movement from the north backed by Iran, seized the capital Sanaa. In 2015 a Saudi-led coalition intervened to support the internationally recognised government. The war has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with hundreds of thousands of deaths from fighting, hunger and disease.
Since 2023 the Houthis have attacked ships in the Red Sea and launched missiles at Israel in solidarity with Gaza, leading to US, British and Israeli strikes.

culture.heading: Ancient heritage
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language, and Yemenis are Muslim, divided between Sunnis (Shafi'i) and Zaydi Shias. Yemen has remarkable architecture: the old city of Sanaa with its decorated tower houses, and Shibam, the "Manhattan of the desert" with mud-brick skyscrapers, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

Chewing qat leaves in afternoon gatherings is a widespread social custom. Saltah, a spicy stew, is the national dish. The jambiya dagger is worn by men as a symbol of status. Socotra island is famous for its unique dragon's blood trees.

politics.heading: Divided country
paragraphs: Yemen is divided. The Houthis control Sanaa and much of the populous north. The internationally recognised government, led by a Presidential Leadership Council, is based in Aden and controls parts of the south and east, but it includes the Southern Transitional Council, which seeks independence for the south. A truce since 2022 has reduced large-scale fighting, but peace talks have stalled.

economy.heading: Humanitarian crisis
paragraphs: Yemen was the poorest country in the Arab world even before the war. The conflict has destroyed infrastructure, collapsed public services and caused widespread food insecurity; most of the population depends on humanitarian aid. Oil and gas exports have largely stopped. The rival authorities use different versions of the rial, which has collapsed in value in government-held areas.
